GS.rationale: Goldman Sachs shows strong fundamental health and positive trajectory. Q1 2026 revenue of $17.23B grew 14.4% YoY with EPS of $17.55 (up 24.3% YoY), driven by a 48% surge in investment banking fees to $2.84B and robust trading activity. The firm is executing a disciplined refocus on its core institutional franchise—Global Banking & Markets and Asset & Wealth Management—while exiting lower-return consumer activities. ROE improved to 14.7% (from ~12% a year ago), and net margin expanded to 29.9%. The investment banking backlog is at multi-year highs, providing visibility into future fee generation. However, balance sheet leverage is high (total liabilities $1.94T vs equity $122.8B), operating cash flow was deeply negative at -$31.87B in Q1 (typical for GS's trading-book dynamics but still a risk factor), and the TTM data is incomplete due to a fiscal reporting gap, limiting full-cycle assessment. On valuation, the stock trades at a P/E of 17.2x, near the top of its 12-month range (13.1–18.4x), and P/B of 2.53x is at the high end of its 1.6–2.5x window—suggesting the market has already priced in much of the earnings recovery. This caps the upside from a pure valuation standpoint. The near-term catalyst is credible: Goldman was named lead underwriter for SpaceX's potentially record-breaking IPO (targeting $75B+ raise at $1.75T valuation in June 2026), which could generate over $1B in underwriting fees and has already driven a 5.8% stock pop. Combined with a record M&A pipeline and expectations for continued capital markets recovery, this provides a modest positive tilt. The score of +0.35 reflects solid fundamentals and a real near-term catalyst, tempered by valuation that is no longer cheap versus its own recent history.
